passage.title: 世界大战
passage.author: H. G. Wells
passage.text: Here and there I found traces of the little people in the shape of rare fossils broken to pieces or threaded in strings upon reeds. And the cases had in some instances been bodily removed—by the Morlocks, as I judged. Weena, who had been rolling a sea urchin down the sloping glass of a case, presently came, as I stared about me, and very quietly took my hand and stood beside me. To me, at least in my present circumstances, these would be vastly more interesting than this spectacle of old-time geology in decay. This appeared to be devoted to minerals, and the sight of a block of sulphur set my mind running on gunpowder. As for the rest of the contents of that gallery, though on the whole they were the best preserved of all I saw, I had little interest. I am no specialist in mineralogy, and I went on down a very ruinous aisle running parallel to the first hall I had entered.
